subject: MAP: load test & dedicated sizing — scheduling and responsibilities
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@acme-retail.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: load test & dedicated sizing — scheduling and responsibilities

Hi Asha / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the MAP milestone focused on load/performance testing and dedicated capacity sizing. Goal is to lock the test window and responsibilities so we can generate a dedicated sizing estimate and run traffic replay at representative QPS.

Summary of ask from Acme:
- Validate peak QPS and P50/P95 latency under near-production traffic (traffic replay)
- Confirm whether Redwood Dedicated pool is required for sustained throughput during the test
- Deliver a post-test report with latency/throughput curves and recommended pool size

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) Pre-test: Acme provides 72 hours of representative request logs + schema mapping (owner: Acme, due: 2026-06-15)
2) Sizing estimate: Redwood to propose dedicated pool sizing and fallback options (owner: Redwood - Dev Patel, due: 2026-06-17)
3) Traffic replay dry-run: small sample window to validate replay tooling (owner: Redwood - Dev Patel, due: 2026-06-19)
4) Full replay + soak test: two-day window with peak windows replayed (owner: joint; Redwood runs, Acme monitors; target dates: 2026-06-21 to 2026-06-22)
5) Post-test analysis & recommendation: Redwood delivers report and recommended Dedicated config (owner: Redwood, due: 2026-06-25)

Immediate asks from our side:
- Confirm whether the June 21–22 window works for Acme (we can shift +/- 3 days)
- Provide a named SRE/eng contact who will push logs and approve test run (we need credentials and sample logs by 2026-06-15)
- Any compliance gating (SOC2 artifacts or data handling rules) that would affect test data location/networking

Attached: traffic_replay_plan.csv (sample columns & replay knobs). I also added a draft MAP spreadsheet (MAP-v1.3.xlsx) to the shared drive link below.

If that looks good I’ll lock the calendar and route to Dev to produce the sizing estimate.

Best,
Ben

On Mon, Jun 7, 2026 at 9:12 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the MAP milestone focused on load/performance testing and dedicated capacity sizing.

Thanks — adding technical detail and confirmation of responsibilities.

Sizing notes (quick draft):
- From the traffic samples Ben shared, expected peak sustained QPS during promo windows is ~3k QPS (95th percentile burst up to ~5k QPS for ~2 minutes).
- For the replay to be representative we recommend provisioning a Dedicated pool equivalent to 4x A10G instances (or 2x A100-class GPUs) for the soak plus an autoscaling headroom policy for short bursts. That provides headroom for prefix cache warmup and KV caching effects.
- If Acme prefers a cost-conservative approach: run replay on hosted + burst to Dedicated for peak windows — we can simulate sustained throughput with a combination of concurrency knobs and request pacing.

Operational checklist (what we need from Acme):
- Representative request logs (sample CSV + request body) mapped to the Redwood replay schema (deadline: 2026-06-15)
- A test VPC peering/IAM role so our replay runner can ingest logs into Acme’s staging ES (we will not retain logs outside the window)
- Confirmation on whether PII is present and if so whether we should use synthetic tokenization during replay

Run plan:
- Dry-run (2026-06-19): small window to validate schema and replay tooling (Dev runs, Samir invited)
- Full replay (2026-06-21 to 2026-06-22): Redwood executes replay; Acme monitors metrics and can trigger early stop

I’ll prepare the sizing worksheet and push MAP-v1.3.xlsx to the shared Drive by EOD today. Ben — I expect to need ~48–72 hours lead time after we receive logs to secure Dedicated capacity and schedule reserved nodes.

Attachments: MAP-v1.3.xlsx (draft).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks, team — that plan looks good. We’ll target the dates as proposed with the heavy peak replay on June 22. Samir (Acme SRE) will own the log upload and IAM role; Samir’s email is samir.patel@acme-retail.com.

Action items from Acme side:
- Samir to upload representative logs to the shared Drive by 2026-06-15 and confirm via email
- I’ll share the SOC2 high-level attestation PDF with Ben by 2026-06-16
- We approve Redwood to provision Dedicated nodes per the sizing worksheet; please send final cost estimate before provisioning

Ben — please lock calendar invites for the dry-run (Jun 19) and the full replay (Jun 21–22) and include the runbook link. We’ll review the post-test report during the week of June 29.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to the run.
